title: Falcon 9 Cygnus NG-25 (SLC-40)

pad.src: https://ll.thespacedevs.com/2.3.0/launches/d74afbc7-0de5-491c-be05-4e9c31f736ac/ (SLC-40). Elevation is not on the LL2 record; 0 m is an ASSUMPTION.

azimuth_deg.derived: Great-circle bearing from the LL2 SLC-40 pad to the midpoint of the far edge of NAVAREA IV 1141/26 Area B (Cygnus NG-25 hazardous rocket launching). Far-edge vertices 31-57.00N 076-28.00W and 31-51.00N 076-17.00W, the two furthest vertices and an edge of the polygon. Midpoint 31.9000N 76.3750W. Unrounded bearing 46.364 deg, rounded to 46.36. Distance 548.3 km. Non-rotating inclination 50.53 deg. Area A of the same notice is a near-shore box within about 49 km of the pad, including a vertex northwest of the pad, and was not used (its downrange edge bears about 52.04 deg). Not retuned to the factsheet 51.64 deg or to 51.6 deg.

payload_kg.assumption: Fixed, not fitted. Northrop Grumman NG-25 factsheet (G26-22496-FS, public release NG26-1913) lists Cygnus XL launch mass 10,500 kg. The same sheet lists ascent cargo 'up to 5,000 kg' on a separate line. That capacity was not added on top of 10,500 kg. The Starlink fit bounds (13.0-21.6 t) do not apply to this spacecraft. 10,500 kg is the factsheet launch mass, not a weighed NG-25 stack.

insertion_alt_km.src: Northrop Grumman NG-25 factsheet G26-22496-FS: initial orbit altitude 245 km x 245 km. https://sky-brokers.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/NG-25-Mission-factsheet.pdf

apoapsis_alt_km.src: Same factsheet, 245 km x 245 km. Inclination on that sheet is 51.64 deg. The azimuth is the hazard bearing and is not tuned to 51.64 deg.

target.altitude_reference: equatorial-radius (r - 6378.137 km) for SMA; insertion altitude residual uses geodetic altitude

header_notes: ILLUSTRATIVE. PRE-FLIGHT. Cygnus XL NG-25 (S.S. Jim Lovell), Falcon 9, SLC-40, to the ISS. T0 2026-11-29T15:47:00Z. LL2 id d74afbc7-0de5-491c-be05-4e9c31f736ac Go, NET 15:47Z, window fields both 15:47Z, last_updated 2026-11-26T11:44:54Z. SpaceX https://www.spacex.com/launches/ng25 prose targets 10:47 a.m. ET. SOURCE CONFLICT: the page header is the window 10:40-11:00 ET (15:40-16:00Z). Used 15:47Z. Backup 30 Nov 10:24 a.m. ET = 2026-11-30T15:24:00Z. Ninth flight. Landing LZ-40.

Published timeline (SpaceX ng25): Max-Q 1:08, MECO 2:13, stage sep 2:17, flip 2:21, SES-1 2:24, boostback 2:30-3:21, fairing 2:53, entry 6:09-6:26, landing burn 7:24, LZ-40 landing 7:49, SECO-1 8:32, Cygnus XL deploys 14:35.

Target 245 x 245 km is the NG factsheet initial orbit, inclination printed there 51.64 deg. Azimuth 46.36 deg is from NAVAREA IV 1141/26 Area B and is not retuned. Deploy T+875 s is the SpaceX 'Cygnus XL Deploys' mark. Booster recovery is not modelled.

knots.src: https://github.com/shahar603/Telemetry-Data/tree/master/Iridium%20NEXT%207 loft, interpolated on the family surrogate rows at T+133 s. FAMILY stand-in. That flight's MECO was T+146 s.

area_m2.derived: pi*(3.7 m/2)^2, Falcon 9 diameter (vehicle config). Cygnus is inside the fairing until T+173 s; after fairing jettison the drag reference stays the vehicle-config area.

deploy.label: Cygnus XL deploy
deploy.note: SpaceX publishes Cygnus XL deployment at T+14:35. No second-stage restart is on that timeline between SECO-1 (T+8:32) and deploy.

fitted.method: scipy least_squares (TRF, bounded) vs published knots + target orbit
